justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 and the brief via Catalogue Service, Item Management Service, and Digital Asset Adapter for physical and digital cataloguing, alongside Circulation Service and Web Application for self-service portals and circulation workflows.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Search response <800 ms (R-05) is directly targeted by Elasticsearch and Redis Catalog Read-Through Cache. API Gateway uses reactive routing, while RabbitMQ offloads asynchronous notification workloads from critical request paths.
justifications.compatibility: Integration with external systems is explicitly specified: Digital Content Proxy Service connects via HTTPS to Digital Content Provider, Payment Integration Client connects to External Payment Gateway, and Dispatch Adapter Component links to Notification Service.
justifications.usability: Web Application provides dedicated access for both Library Patron and Library Staff via UI Component Library (Radix UI, Tailwind CSS) and modular feature sets, though both user types share a single frontend container.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance is reinforced by Resilience Handler and Provider Client using Resilience4j circuit breaking and retries, RabbitMQ Dead Letter Exchange for failed processing, and PostgreSQL Write-Ahead Log for transaction durability.
justifications.security: EU data residency and GDPR compliance are enforced by Compliance Audit Component and EU-restricted PostgreSQL. Authentication & Authorization Component, Data Sanitizer Component (stripping PII), and Row-Level Security Policy Enforcer provide thorough protection.
justifications.maintainability: The system decomposes cleanly into decoupled microservices (Catalogue Service, Circulation Service, Notification Worker). However, modeling internal vendor processes inside PostgreSQL, Redis, and Elasticsearch at Level 3 introduces unnecessary COTS modeling overhead.
justifications.portability: Services run on standard runtime platforms (Java Spring Boot, Node.js, React). The constraint for EU-only data residency is strictly localized to the PostgreSQL container and supporting cloud deployment environments without platform lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Elasticsearch cluster handles high-volume search queries directly while Redis provides catalog read-through caching and API Gateway handles rate limiting, comfortably keeping P99 response under 800 ms.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch shard sizing and replica count
Redis cache hit ratio for frequent searches
tradeoffs: Read caching in Redis reduces search load but risks serving stale catalog data

PERF-02.justification: Catalogue Service persists writes to PostgreSQL and emits internal events to Search Indexing Service for Elasticsearch updates, keeping writes asynchronous from reads and easily fulfilling the 5-minute index lag.
sensitivity_points: Throughput of in-process search indexing events during high write volumes
tradeoffs: Asynchronous search index syncing prioritizes search query performance over immediate consistency

AVAIL-01.justification: Elasticsearch cluster coordination module manages shard replicas to recover from node failure within seconds. Circulation transactions are entirely independent, persisting to PostgreSQL and remaining completely unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch replica count configuration per index
tradeoffs: Maintaining Elasticsearch replica shards increases infrastructure cost and write overhead

AVAIL-02.justification: Web Application instances are fronted by API Gateway with sessions offloaded to Redis Session Management. Failure of one instance allows traffic to seamlessly route to healthy instances without lost transactions.
sensitivity_points: Upstream health check intervals on the gateway
tradeoffs: Centralizing user sessions in Redis creates an operational dependency on the Redis cache cluster

MOD-01.justification: Digital Content Proxy Service encapsulates vendor communication via the Provider Client component and Digital Asset Adapter, isolating changes necessary for new external providers from the core catalogue.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility of the Provider Client abstraction interface
tradeoffs: Maintaining a separate proxy service adds network latency for content streaming

MOD-02.justification: The Loan Management Component in Circulation Service hardcodes loan rules within Spring Boot services. There is no externalized rule engine, policy engine, or dynamic configuration mechanism to alter rules without redeploying code.
sensitivity_points: Coupling of loan business logic to compiled Java application code
tradeoffs: Hardcoding rules in code ensures compile-time safety but sacrifices operational agility

SEC-01.justification: PostgreSQL data persistence is explicitly constrained to EU regions, and the Compliance Audit Component intercepts writes to enforce residency. Notification Worker's Data Sanitizer strips PII before contacting external services.
sensitivity_points: Coverage of Compliance Audit Component interceptors across all write paths
Hosting region configuration of cloud infrastructure
tradeoffs: Restricting processing and persistence to EU regions limits deployment options and cloud provider flexibility

SEC-02.justification: Authentication and authorization are verified at the API Gateway, while PostgreSQL Row-Level Security Policy Enforcer and the Compliance Audit Component actively intercept unauthorized cross-patron access and record audit trails.
sensitivity_points: Correctness of PostgreSQL row-level security policy predicates
tradeoffs: Enforcing row-level security policies in the database introduces minor query planning overhead
